meta.titre: Child Rights and Child Protection: rights, dangers and the bodies that protect children
meta.sous_theme: Rights of the child, child labour, trafficking, terrorism, refugees and protection

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Citizenship Education past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: In markets and along the roads, some children sell water and fruit during school hours instead of sitting in class. Others are sent far from home to work for strangers, and some flee violence with their families and lose their homes and schools. Children need special care because they are young and cannot defend themselves alone. The GCE tests the rights of the child, the dangers that threaten children, and the people and bodies that protect them.

items: In the international law on children, a child is a person below the age of eighteen.
A right is something that every person may claim simply because he or she is a human being.
Parents have the first duty to feed, clothe, educate and protect their children.

sections.titre: Rights of the child and threats to children
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Rights of the child
The rights of children are set out in the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child and in the African Charter on the Rights and Welfare of the Child, and they are protected by the laws of Cameroon. They can be grouped as follows.

| Group | Examples |
|---|---|
| Survival | Life, food, shelter, clean water and health care |
| Development | Education, play and leisure, a name and a nationality |
| Protection | Protection from abuse, neglect, harmful work, trafficking and the effects of war |
| Participation | The right to express opinions and to be heard in matters that concern the child |

### Dangers that threaten children
Child labour is work that harms the health, education or development of a child. Light help at home that does not harm school or health is not child labour. Child trafficking is the recruiting, moving or receiving of children in order to exploit them. Terrorism is the use of violence or threats to spread fear in order to force a political aim. Refugees are people who flee from their country because of war, persecution or violence and seek safety in another country.

| Danger | Causes | Manifestations |
|---|---|---|
| Child labour | Poverty, orphanhood, ignorance, large families, weak enforcement of laws | Children hawking during school hours, working on farms, in mines or as house helps, tired and absent from class |
| Child trafficking | Poverty, false promises of a better life, demand for cheap workers, weak border control | Children taken away from their families, forced work or begging, no schooling, abuse |
| Terrorism | Extremist ideas, unemployment and poverty, easy access to weapons | Killings, kidnappings, destruction, school closures, families forced to flee |
| Refugees | War, persecution, violence | Camps, overcrowding, shortage of food and health care, children separated from their families |

### Who protects children?
Parents and the family come first. The State protects children through laws, courts and the police and through ministries, for example the ministry in charge of social affairs, which cares for vulnerable people and for children in conflict with the law, and the ministry in charge of women's empowerment and the family. International bodies such as UNICEF defend the rights of children, and the UN refugee agency, UNHCR, assists refugees. Non-governmental organisations, schools and churches also help. The Day of the African Child is celebrated on 16 June.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When you must treat two or more dangers, each in its own paragraph
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give each danger a heading, then write 'Causes:' with two or three explained points and 'Manifestations:' with two or three visible signs. Never put a cause in the manifestations or the reverse. Divide the marks and the time equally.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a situation is described and one right must be named
variantes.contenu_markdown: Ask what the child loses. Hawking in school hours harms education and rest; hazardous work harms health; having no birth certificate harms the right to a name and a nationality; being forced to work for strangers harms protection.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks for institutions or persons
variantes.contenu_markdown: Move from the closest to the farthest: parents and family, school and community, the State (law, courts, police, ministries), then international bodies such as UNICEF. Name each and say what it does.

sections.enonce_markdown: Write the model answer to this question: Define child labour, then give two causes and two manifestations of it. [6 marks]

etapes.justification: There are three tasks: a definition, causes and manifestations. Each must be kept in its own place.
A good definition says what the work does to the child.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Child labour is work done by a child that harms the health, education or development of the child.

etapes.justification: Causes are the reasons why children work.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Poverty in the family; the death of parents or ignorance of the value of education.

etapes.justification: Manifestations are what can be seen.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Children hawking during school hours; children working on farms or in other heavy jobs.

etapes.action: Link each point to a short explanation.
etapes.justification: An explanation turns a bare list into marks.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Poor families need extra income; orphaned children must support themselves; hawking keeps children out of school.

sections.conclusion_markdown:
Child labour is work done by a child that harms the child's health, education or development.

Causes: first, poverty, because a family that cannot meet its needs sends its children to earn money; second, the death of parents or ignorance, because orphans must support themselves and some parents do not see the value of school.

Manifestations: first, children hawking goods in markets and streets during school hours, which keeps them out of class; second, children doing heavy work on farms or in other jobs, which tires them and can injure them.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: 'Child labour means any work done by a child, even helping parents at home.'
items.pourquoi_faux: Light help at home that does not harm school or health is part of normal upbringing. Child labour harms the child.
items.correction_markdown: Child labour is work that harms the health, education or development of the child.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: 'Rights mean that children may do whatever they like.'
items.pourquoi_faux: Rights are protections and opportunities that must be used with respect for others. Children also have duties, such as respecting parents and studying.
items.correction_markdown: Children's rights guarantee survival, development, protection and participation, and go with responsibilities.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: 'Refugees are people who move from one town to another inside their country.'
items.pourquoi_faux: Refugees leave their country and cross a border. People who flee but stay in their country are internally displaced.
items.correction_markdown: Refugees are people who flee to another country because of war, persecution or violence.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes: 'If the parents agree, sending a child to work for strangers is not trafficking.'
items.pourquoi_faux: A parent's agreement does not make exploitation lawful, especially when the child is deceived or forced to work.
items.correction_markdown: Child trafficking is moving or receiving children for exploitation, even when a parent was persuaded by false promises.

items.erreur_markdown: Asked for the causes of child labour, a student writes: 'children hawking in the streets'.
items.pourquoi_faux: This is a manifestation, something that can be seen, not a cause.
items.correction_markdown: Give causes such as poverty, orphanhood and weak enforcement of the laws.

items.enonce_markdown: Say whether each right belongs to the group survival, development, protection or participation: (a) clean water; (b) going to school; (c) not being forced to work in a dangerous mine; (d) giving an opinion on matters that concern the child.

In an invented market district, a survey of 240 children aged 6 to 14 finds that 36 of them hawk goods during school hours. (a) Calculate the percentage of these children. (b) Name the right that is mainly violated. (c) Give two actions that can reduce the problem.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) 36 / 240 x 100 = **15%**.

(b) The right to education, and also the rights to rest and play and to health.

(c) Award marks for two valid actions, for example: help poor families with income so that children need not work; enforce the laws on child labour and school attendance; make education affordable; run campaigns to teach parents the value of school.

items.enonce_markdown: Many children in a border town have disappeared after accepting offers of 'a better life' in another city. (a) Explain two causes of child trafficking. (b) Explain three measures that parents, the community and the State can take to protect children against it.
items.solution_markdown:
Award marks for developed points.

(a) Causes: poverty, because families accept offers that seem to promise food, school or money; false promises of recruiters, who deceive parents and children; also weak control of borders and demand for cheap workers.

(b) Measures: parents should know the people who take their children and refuse offers that are not clear; the community should watch strangers who move with children and report suspicious cases to the police or social services; the State should punish traffickers, control borders and transport routes, support poor families, register births and bring trafficked children back to school. Other valid measures: awareness campaigns and the work of NGOs.

**Protection works when family, community and State act together.**

items_markdown: The rights of the child can be grouped as survival, development, protection and participation.
Child labour is harmful work done by a child; it violates the rights to education, health, rest and play.
Child trafficking is the recruiting and moving of children to exploit them; refugees are people who flee across a border from war or persecution.
For each danger, keep causes (why it happens) separate from manifestations (what is seen).
Children are protected by parents, the State through laws, courts and ministries such as social affairs, and international bodies such as UNICEF and UNHCR.
The Day of the African Child is celebrated on 16 June.
